title: Right for the age, never childish
statement: Design each student screen for its learners' age without infantilizing them: no childish visuals or wording, and no clutter, pop-ups or decoration that obscures learning.
detail: The golden student-course standard asks of every student-facing surface whether the visual experience feels coherent and appropriate for the intended learner while preserving rigour, so that design supports attention, confidence and meaning rather than looking like a review document or empty decoration. It accepts a surface when hierarchy, density, typography, imagery, motion and interaction language are coherent for that learner, and lists infantilization among its failure signals beside placeholder imagery, diagnostic clutter, tiny evidence, competing styles and decorative media that obscures learning. Its claim boundary makes no single map, character, colour, layout or visual metaphor mandatory.
against: This is qualitative usability research, not learning outcomes, and the figures come from the free summary article because the full report is paywalled (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/design/grade-9/research/learners-voice-guide.md`, line 102; `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/design/grade-9/research/edtech-desktop-design.md`, line 115).

evidence.quote: Visual design supports attention, confidence, and meaning rather than looking like a review document or empty decoration.
Hierarchy, density, typography, imagery, motion, and interaction language are coherent for the intended learner;
Placeholder imagery; diagnostic clutter; infantilization; tiny evidence; competing styles; decorative media that obscures learning.
No single map, character, color, layout, or visual metaphor is mandatory.
NN/g found the word "kid" works as a "teen repellent."
Teens show "dramatically lower levels of patience" and dislike overused animation, small fonts, forced sharing and pop-ups.
They dislike both childish graphics and "cluttered screen[s] full of text", and dislike pointless multimedia and auto-play.
NN/g: avoid babyish visuals, the word "kid", condescending copy, clutter, auto-play and gratuitous animation.
They want "small, meaningful chunks with plenty of white space".
No mascot art, no fly-in celebrations, one accent colour.
